pr_title: sql: rewrite index backfiller to stream back progress
pr_body:
Previously, the DistSQL version index backfiller did a a few things
which were non-idiomatic:

- There was fixed time duration and a buffer fill threshold at which the
  backfiller would stop constructing/ingesting index entries and update
the job with its progress. This would potentially cause the DistSQL flow
to get planned, run and tore down multiple times within a single index
backfill schema change.

- The index backfiller relied on the chunk backfiller which performed
  all operations on a fixed "chunk" of rows at a time. Future plans to
make this a memory account/dynamically changing unit of operation meant
that we had to move away from this model.

The new index backfiller logic takes inspiration from our import
coordinator and processors setup. In general, the DistSQL flow is setup
once and the various processors are assigned the spans to backfill.
Every processor concurrently constructs one or more "index entry batch"
and ingests the associated KVs. Periodic go routines stream back the
completed spans to the coordinator node, which in turn periodically
writes the fraction progressed and remaining spans (to account for job
resumption) to the schema change job.

While the size of the index entries in a batch is currently fixed,
future work to be memory aware via the index backfiller mem monitor
should not be particularly difficult to add.

It is important to note that the core index entry building logic has not
been changed. Neither has the column backfiller or the logic for index
backfilling in a txn.

Fixes: #54528

Release note: None

issue_context.title: sql, bulk: rewrite index backfiller
issue_context.body:
Currently it does fixed size batches, and also starts/stops regularly for progress reporting.

Instead, we could look more like IMPORT: produce in small batches, stream and flush as needed, return async progress as we go, etc. Sitting on the old backfiller / chunkbacfiller is probably doing more harm than good now and a scratch rewrite of the build index piece could make it smaller, more reliable and faster.

review_comments: Is not observing changes in table desc version throughout an index backfill okay? This was not the case in the old implementation as we would re-acquire the table desc lease after every 2mins/80% buffer fill as part of the DistSQL flow planning. This in turn would throw a version mismatch error and our schema change would be retried.
I'll defer to @lucy-zhang or @ajwerner on this one.
